transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Redwood Solutions), Nora Blake (Lark Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (Eng Manager), Priya Rao (Product), Alex Kim (Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Nora: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Samira.
[00:07] Samira: Awesome, quick agenda: walk through Redwood Eval / Quality Monitoring, show prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B comparison flows in the Console, and how you can hook this up to the API/Optimize for active pilots. Then Q&A and next steps.
[00:20] Carlos: Sounds good. We're specifically trying to detect regressions after model updates and compare two prompt variants at scale.
[00:27] Ethan: Great, that's what we'll focus on. I'll share my screen — give me one sec.
[00:33] [screen share starts]
[00:40] Ethan: Ok so this is the Redwood Console, main evals page. At the top you can see prompt sets — you can upload CSVs or connect via our API. Most teams upload a representative prompt set per intent, and we version them.
[00:58] Priya: Quick question — can prompt sets include metadata like intent tags and expected outputs?
[01:05] Ethan: Yes. You can attach tags, expected outputs, acceptance criteria, and preferred parsing rules. We also store the assertion logic as a small script or JSON schema. Sometimes the transcription shows a little mismatch — uh, sorry, sometimes the exported schema name appears as "asertion" in older uploads, but the UI normalizes that.
[01:30] Nora: Hmm, is there a way to automatically run those prompt sets against production traffic or only on stored samples?
[01:36] Ethan: Both. You can run offline batch evals against historical logs, or you can enable a live sampling hook that sends a subset of production requests to the eval pipeline — with sampling rate controls to protect PII. For Lark you might want a low-sample live feed first.
[01:56] Alex: On that note, how is PII handled? We need to know about encryption, KMS, and retention.
[02:02] Maya: Good question. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated. For hosted, data-in-transit is TLS and at-rest is encrypted with our managed keys; we can provide SOC2 controls and an encryption whitepaper. We'll attach those to the follow-up.
[02:21] Alex: Please do. Also any redaction step before it hits Redwood?
[02:25] Ethan: We offer pre-ingest redaction hooks and client-side redaction samples. For live sampling, you can apply redaction rules at your edge before we receive calls.
[02:33] [00:03] Carlos: Back to regressions — show us how alerts work.
[02:38] Ethan: Sure — jumping to the Alerts tab. You can set regression alerts on any metric: token-level perplexity proxies, exact match rate, semantic similarity thresholds, and custom eval functions. Alerts support thresholds, rolling windows, and canary detection between two model versions or two prompt variants.
[02:58] Priya: Can we configure A/B comparisons automatically as part of a rollout?
[03:03] Ethan: Yes. In the rollouts panel you can create an A/B test: define traffic split, tie each variant to a model or prompt set, and pick the eval metric you're optimizing. The Console will show a head-to-head comparison with confidence intervals and automatic significance tests.
[03:21] Nora: Nice. If we see a regression, can we auto-fallback to previous model?
[03:26] Ethan: Absolutely. You can define automated policies: if the primary model drops below a threshold for X minutes, route traffic to the fallback model and trigger a notification. We log the event and surface it in trace view.
[03:39] Carlos: How does this integrate with the API and Optimize?
[03:44] Ethan: Two parts — API integration and Optimize recommendations. For API integration, you can attach an eval profile to an API route so every call — or sampled calls — are scored by the eval pipeline and logged. For Optimize, we analyze traffic patterns and suggest batching, quantization profiles, or model variants to meet a cost/latency tradeoff for your workload. That recommendation engine can also propose candidate prompt variants for A/B testing based on historical success rates.
[04:10] Priya: Does Optimize suggest prompt edits or only model/quantization settings?
[04:14] Ethan: Both. We have a prompt tuning suggestion feature — it identifies prompts that produce high variance and proposes safer templates; you can accept suggestions and push them to a new prompt set. We also have model selection and quantization recommendations.
[04:29] Samira: I'll jump in with a high-level example — imagine you roll a new model and your FAQ generator's exact match drops from 82% to 68% after deploy. With Redwood you can detect that via an alert, automatically run a targeted A/B to confirm, and then either rollback or route to a fallback while a patch/prompt tweak is tested.
[04:52] Nora: That scenario is exactly our concern. We had a recent rollout where entity extraction regressed on medical terms.
[04:59] Ethan: Right, and we can scope an eval to focus on those entity types — tag prompts by entity set and run precision/recall metrics.
[05:09] Carlos: Can we store golden answers for sensitive prompts so they never leave our VPC?
[05:14] Maya: For Private deployments or Dedicated with VPC, yes — golden sets can remain in your storage and we run the eval compute in the customer tenancy. For hosted, we support encrypted attachments and minimal retention options but if you need strict isolation we'd recommend Dedicated or Private.
[05:31] Alex: What's the latency impact if we enable live eval sampling on the API route?
[05:36] Ethan: The eval scoring happens asynchronously; the API path returns as usual. For synchronous checks we can do a fast pre-check but that adds around 20-50 ms depending on metric and model. For most customers we prefer async with sampling.
[05:51] Priya: Walk us through setting up a regression alert end-to-end?
[05:55] Ethan: Sure — quick demo: create an eval project, upload a prompt set CSV, label expectations, pick metric (e.g., semantic-sim >0.85), set baseline model and comparison model, define window (24h) and sensitivity (low/med/high). Then add notification channels (Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks) and auto-actions (rollback after 3 triggers).
[06:20] Ethan: I'll now show an A/B run we had for a retail customer — you'll see the comparison chart, p-values, and the automated recommendation. Note sometimes the axis labels exported to CSV used a different timezone — small export quirks in older releases, we're patching that in next minor.
[06:51] Nora: Are there sample templates for our medical use-cases so we don't start from scratch?
[06:55] Samira: Yes — we have industry templates (healthcare, finance, retail) with common prompt sets, entity lists, and metric presets. We'll include the healthcare template in the follow-up.
[07:07] Carlos: Ok, show me the API payload — how do we send logs and attach eval metadata?
[07:12] Ethan: Over here — the API accepts a JSON payload with prompt, model, route, and optional metadata fields. You can also attach a prompt_id that maps to a prompt set entry. For large-scale uploads we support batch CSV ingestion. Example payloads are in our SDK.
[07:29] Priya: One more on the A/B: can we automatically promote the winning variant?
[07:33] Ethan: You can enable automatic promotion with guardrails — require a minimum traffic volume and significance level. If criteria met, the rollout flips and we log the change with a trace id.
[07:45] Nora: Great. Security again — can we get a private demo of Dedicated deployment and how KMS integrates?
[07:51] Samira: Absolutely, that's a good next step. We'll set a Dedicated deep-dive with our infra PM and security lead.
[07:59] Alex: Also need SAML/SSO and RBAC details.
[08:03] Maya: We support SAML, SCIM for user provisioning, fine-grained RBAC with per-route permissions, and audit logs exported to your SIEM. We'll send the security pack.
[08:14] Carlos: For the pilot, what's a reasonable scope? 2 intents, 1k prompts each, run against 1 week of logs?
[08:21] Samira: Yep that's reasonable. Typical pilot is 1-3 intents, a 1-2k prompt set, and a 1-2 week historical run plus live sampling. We can also run a perf benchmark with your sample to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[08:34] Nora: Costs — how do we estimate the eval compute cost?
[08:38] Ethan: We price eval runs per-eval unit derived from model size, sequence length, and eval function complexity. For pilots we often provide credits; for Dedicated you get reserved compute. We'll include a cost model example in the follow-up.
[08:53] Priya: If we do A/B with two models, do we pay double?
[08:57] Ethan: You pay for the tokens/compute used per variant; Optimize can suggest cheaper model variants to test while keeping quality constraints. Also you can sample fewer traffic for each variant to reduce cost while retaining statistical power.
[09:12] Samira: Quick recap — Redwood can: version prompt sets, run offline/online evals, alert on regressions with auto-actions, run A/B with significance tests, and feed Optimize to get cost/latency recommendations. We'll send templates, security docs, and a recommended pilot plan.
[09:34] Nora: That covers most of it. Two blockers: security docs and making sure golden data stays in our VPC.
[09:41] Samira: Understood — Dedicated deep-dive and security pack. We'll mark those as follow-ups.
[09:47] Carlos: One last practical: how long to stand up a pilot?
[09:50] Ethan: Once we have sample prompts and a small log export, we can spin up a pilot environment in 3-5 business days for Hosted, and 2-4 weeks for Dedicated provisioning.
[10:02] Priya: Perfect.
[10:04] Alex: A quick question about data residency — our customers in EU require data to remain in EU. Can Redwood route evals to region-specific compute?
[10:11] Maya: Yes, we have region-aware routing and you can pin eval projects to a region. For strict residency Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[10:18] Nora: Alright, sounds good. Appreciate the demo.
[10:21] Samira: Thanks Nora. We'll follow up with the deck, templates, security docs, and the pilot checklist.
[10:27] Closing: confirm next steps and owners.
[10:30] END

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "asertion" vs "assertion"), timestamps approximate. Some speaker labels are role-based.
